shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading 1×A for 1×B would make my inventory less balanced (A:0, B:2, C:1). Since I value variety, this reduces my utility.
Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1 B for 1 A would create 2A/0B/1C, reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced, so it lowers my utility.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (3,0,1). Since goods are equally valued and I prefer variety, this reduces variety by eliminating B, so it lowers my utility.
Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading 1C for 1B would create imbalance (1A/2B/0C). Since I value variety and currently all goods are equally represented, this decreases my utility.
Starting from an even 1A,1B,1C bundle, trading 1 B for 1 C would make my inventory less balanced (1A,0B,2C). Since I value variety and currently value all goods equally, this lowers my utility.
Starting from an even bundle (1A,1B,1C), giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory to 1A,0B,3C. This increases my total goods and is favorable for utility based only on this exchange.
Trading 1 A for 1 B would change my balanced inventory from (1,1,1) to (0,2,1), reducing variety, which lowers my utility.
I value A, B, and C equally, and this trade would change my balanced inventory from 1A/1B/1C to 2A/0B/1C, reducing variety and making my bundle less useful to me.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A leaves me with A:3, B:0, C:1. Since I value variety and goods are otherwise equal, gaining more total goods outweighs the loss of some balance, so this increases my utility.

Starting from an even bundle of 1A, 1B, 1C, exchanging 1C for 1B would make my inventory less balanced (1A, 2B, 0C). Since I value variety and currently hold all goods equally, this lowers my utility.
Starting from an even bundle (1A, 1B, 1C), trading 1B for 1C would make my inventory less balanced (1A, 0B, 2C). Since I value variety and currently value scarcer goods more, this reduces my utility.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (1,0,3). This increases my total goods and gives me more of a good at the cost of one unit of another, which improves my bundle overall.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from (A2,B1,C1) to (A1,B2,C1), which keeps totals balanced and improves variety by reducing my most-held good. The market note that B is harder to obtain also makes receiving B favorable.

Giving up my only B for an A would reduce variety-adjusted utility: after the trade I would have A=3, B=0, C=1, making my scarcest good disappear. The market update also says B is harder to obtain, increasing the opportunity cost of giving it away.

Giving 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C. Since I value variety and currently have the most A, some A is less valuable than B, but sacrificing all of my A for a second B makes my bundle less balanced overall.
Giving up my only B would reduce variety and B is currently more scarce in the market, so 2A for 1B does not improve my bundle.

Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A2,B1,C1) to (A2,B2,C0), which reduces variety because I lose one of my scarcer goods and increase a good I already have. Since I value goods equally and prefer balance, this does not increase my utility.
Giving up my only B for an extra C would reduce variety and is especially unfavorable because B is currently harder to obtain.
Giving up my only B would reduce variety and is especially costly since B is currently scarce. Receiving 2 C would leave me with a less balanced bundle, so this trade does not improve my utility.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves variety by filling my current shortage of B. My inventory would move from A2,B0,C2 to A1,B1,C2, which better matches my preference for balanced holdings.
This trade increases variety in my inventory by converting surplus A into scarce B. Moving from (A2,B0,C2) to (A0,B1,C2) improves balance, and B is currently harder to obtain.
Receiving 1 B and giving 1 C improves my variety: I currently have no B, so B is more valuable to me than an additional C. The market update that B is harder to obtain further supports accepting.

I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B significantly improves variety. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus good relative to B, and the market update suggests B is becoming harder to obtain, increasing the value of receiving it now.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from A1/B1/C2 to A0/B2/C2. Since I value variety and currently have no surplus of A over B, this does not improve balance. However, B is becoming harder to obtain, so receiving B is at least as valuable as giving A, making this trade acceptable.

Giving up 1 B for 1 A would reduce variety-adjusted utility: my inventory would go from A1,B1,C2 to A2,B0,C2, making B my scarcest good and especially valuable. The market bulletin also indicates B is harder to obtain, further weakening this trade for me.

Giving up my only B is unfavorable because B is currently scarce in the market, and after the trade my bundle would become less balanced (A:3, B:0, C:2). The extra A does not outweigh losing all of my B.
Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from A1/B1/C2 to A1/B2/C1, which is more balanced and keeps variety high. It also gives me an additional unit of the currently harder-to-obtain good B.
Giving up 1 B for 1 C would reduce variety in my inventory. I currently have fewer A and B than C, and B is also harder to obtain in the market, so trading B away for more C lowers my utility.

Trading 2 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C2) to (A1,B2,C0). Since I currently have the most C and B is also becoming scarcer, exchanging surplus C for B is a reasonable improvement in this trade.
Giving up my only B would reduce variety and B is currently harder to obtain, while receiving more of the good I already have most does not improve my bundle.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by converting a surplus good into one I currently lack, and B is especially valuable right now.
This trade increases variety by converting surplus A into scarce B. My inventory would move from A2,B0,C2 to A0,B1,C2, which better balances my holdings, and B is currently harder to obtain.

Receiving 1 B and giving 1 C improves my variety: I currently have no B, so B is more valuable to me than an extra C. The market bulletin also indicates B is harder to obtain, which further supports accepting.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B strongly improves variety. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus good and results in a more balanced bundle, which increases my utility despite B being harder to obtain.
I currently have no B and some A, so exchanging 1 A for 1 B increases the variety and balance of my inventory, which improves my utility.
B is currently valuable because I have none, but giving 2 A for 1 B reduces my overall bundle too much; a 2-for-1 exchange is not a utility gain for me.
This trade improves variety in my inventory by converting a surplus C into a missing B, which increases my utility.
B is valuable because I currently have none, but giving 2 C for 1 B reduces my overall variety-adjusted utility too much; 1-for-1 would be more balanced.
Trading 1 A for 1 B increases variety in my inventory, moving from A:2,B:0,C:2 to A:1,B:1,C:2. Since I value scarcer goods more, gaining B while reducing a surplus A improves my bundle.
This would reduce my variety by taking all 2 of my A for only 1 B, leaving me with 0 A, 1 B, and 2 C. Since I value goods equally but prefer balanced holdings, this lowers my utility.
I currently have no B and already have 2 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B increases variety and improves my bundle.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B increases variety and balances my inventory. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus relative to B, leaving me with a more even bundle overall.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves variety: B is currently my scarcest good, while I have more A, so this increases my utility.
B is currently valuable because I have none, but giving 2×A for only 1×B reduces my overall bundle too much. The variety gain does not outweigh losing two units of A.
I currently have no B and a surplus of C, so trading 1 C for 1 B increases variety and improves my bundle.
I currently lack B entirely, so gaining 1 B increases variety significantly. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus good, and the resulting bundle is more balanced overall.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves variety: I currently have no B and extra A, so gaining B and reducing A increases my utility.
Giving 2×A to receive 1×B would leave me with a less balanced bundle overall. Although B is currently scarce for me, this exchange costs too much A for only 1×B and does not improve my utility.
Trading 1 C for 1 B increases variety in my inventory by gaining a good I currently lack and reducing a surplus good, so it improves my utility.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B increases variety significantly. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus relative to B, and the resulting bundle is more balanced.
